source_edits.role: Hardened Telegram Mini App authentication module with IETF language_code subtags and exhaustive C0/DEL control character rejection
Comprehensive 37-test golden and negative verification suite including signed pt-BR, es-419 vectors and C0/DEL control tests

corrections_applied: IETF BCP-47 language_code validation: is_valid_language_code accepts bounded ASCII alphanumeric hyphen-separated subtags (max 64 bytes total, each subtag 1..8 characters, first subtag letters only). Admitted legitimate subtags include pt-BR, zh-Hant, and es-419, while malformed codes and underscore-delimited codes (such as EN_US) remain rejected.

Exhaustive C0 control and DEL character rejection: updated contains_disallowed_bytes and is_valid_parameter_value to inspect codepoints using string.to_utf_codepoints and string.utf_codepoint_to_int, rejecting all C0 control characters (codepoints 0 to 31, including NUL, CR, LF, ESC, BEL, TAB) and DEL (codepoint 127).
Parameter key validation consolidation: is_valid_parameter_key utilizes is_ascii_alphanumeric with underscore exemption for strict [a-zA-Z0-9_] 1..64 byte ASCII identifiers.
Expanded test suite: added signed positive vectors for pt-BR and es-419, plus negative tests for C0 control characters and DEL (0x7F) in parameter values.

process_and_provenance_notes.compilation_strategy: gleam compile-package in isolated recovery runtime, beams linked directly into dev ebin
process_and_provenance_notes.tooling_truth: Source edits were written via direct agent write tools (write_to_file, replace_file_content) and file inspections were performed via direct read/grep tools; compilations and test suite executions were mediated by the OTP 29 development:bounded Erlang harness. ZERO Python executed.
